channels.regime: Strong PMI/new orders and rising prices reinforce the Fed's hawkish stance.
US 10Y ~5.10%, real 10Y ~2.78%, strong USD, weak Treasury auction and Japan 10Y at 3.055% show a global duration shock.
AI/project-finance dispersion and private-credit concerns remain active; fresh CCC OAS is a gap.
Strong PMI and AI physical demand support funded capex, but financing/permitting filters tighten.
Crude rebounded after five declines; no return yet to peak war-premium regime.
Diesel futures fell to a two-week low, but policy distortion and expensive STS freight complicate the signal.
Broad equities fell on Sep 23 and TradingView's Top Stories explicitly flags a narrowing AI rally.
Gold is tactically pressured by stronger USD and sharply higher real yields.
SoftBank's US$11.1B bond deal proves funding access for a strong sponsor but reinforces leverage and credit-market dependence.
Trade truce reduces tail risk but does not itself prove domestic-demand repair.
Rare earths remain a central US-China negotiating and aerospace supply-security issue.
Texas/EU constraints and self-supply requirements keep realizable MW below headline queues.

notes: The Sep 23 PMI release invalidated the prior tactical assumption that lower crude would keep the US 10Y contained below 5%.
The Sep 24 Japan move broadens the rates problem: 10Y JGB 3.055% and 30Y 4.125% raise the risk of global duration repricing and Japanese capital repatriation.
Real yields remain the cleanest cross-asset constraint: ~2.78% US 10Y TIPS raises the hurdle for gold, long-duration equities and leveraged infrastructure.
Do not interpret SoftBank's successful bond sale as broad AI-credit normalization; it confirms capital availability for strong sponsors while leverage rises.
Crude and diesel diverged on Sep 23; keep crude, product cracks and freight as separate signals.
Creator/social claims remain zero-weight until independently verified.

forwardView.baseCase: Rates remain the dominant cross-asset constraint unless the 7Y auction/Fed communication reverses the Sep 23 move. Japan now reinforces rather than offsets the global duration shock. AI can remain fundamentally strong while equity breadth and project finance weaken.
forwardView.dollar: Bias firm while US growth/prices and front-end yields remain strong; weak yen adds imported-inflation pressure in Japan.
forwardView.rates: 5% US 10Y is no longer merely a test; sustained US real-yield pressure plus Japan 10Y above 3% is the key valuation regime variable.
forwardView.equities: Prefer funded cash-generative AI infrastructure and selective cybersecurity; require breadth/credit confirmation before broad risk-on.
forwardView.energy: Separate crude rebound from diesel/product/freight normalization; policy headlines can distort product futures.
forwardView.gold: Tactically weak until real yields and DXY roll over together.
forwardView.nextCatalyst: Trump-Xi summit, US $44B 7Y Treasury auction, Fed speakers and follow-through in JGB yields on Sep 24.
